source_text: Ὁ ἔπαρχος λέγει πρὸς τὸν Ἰουστῖνον· Ἄκουε, ὁ λεγόμενος λόγιος καὶ νομίζων ἀληθινοὺς εἰδέναι λόγους. Ἐὰν μαστιγωθεὶς ἀποκεφαλισθῇς, πέπεισαι ὅτι μέλλεις ἀναβαίνειν εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν; Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Ἐλπίζω ἕξειν αὐτοῦ τὰ δώματα, ἐὰν ὑπομείνω ταῦτα. Οἶδα γὰρ πᾶσι τοῖς οὕτω βιώσασι παραμένειν τὸ θεῖον χάρισμα μέχρι τῆς ἐκπληρώσεως τοῦ παντὸς κόσμου. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπεν· Σὺ οὖν ὑπονοεῖς ὅτι ἀναβήσῃ εἰς τοὺς οὐρανούς, ἀμοιβὰς τινας ἀποληψόμενος; Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Οὐχ ὑπονοῶ, ἀλλ᾽ ἐπίσταμαι καὶ πεπληροφόρημαι. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπεν· Τὸ λοιπὸν ἔλθωμεν εἰς τὸ προκείμενον καὶ κατεπεῖγον πρᾶγμα. Συνελθόντες οὖν ὁμοθυμαδὸν θύσατε τοῖς θεοῖς. Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Οὐδεὶς εὖ φρονῶν ἀπὸ εὐσεβείας εἰς ἀσέβειαν μεταπίπτει. Ὁ Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπεν· Εἰ μὴ πείθεσθε, τιμωρηθήσεσθε ἀνηλεῶς. Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Ἃν εὐχῆς ἔχωμεν διὰ τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν τιμωρηθέντες σωθῆναι, ὅτι τοῦτο ἡμῖν σωτηρία καὶ παρρησία γενήσεται ἐπὶ τοῦ φοβερωτέρου καὶ παγκοσμίου βήματος τοῦ δεσπότου ἡμῶν καὶ σωτῆρος. Ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ μάρτυρες εἶπον· Ποίει ὃ θέλεις. Ἡμεῖς γὰρ Χριστιανοί ἐσμεν καὶ εἰδώλοις οὐ θύομεν. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος ἀπεφήνατο λέγων· Οἱ μὴ βουληθέντες θῦσαι τοῖς θεοῖς καὶ εἶξαι τῷ τοῦ αὐτοκράτορος προστάγματι μαστιγωθέντες ἀπαχθήτωσαν, κεφαλικὴν ἀποτιννύντες δίκην κατὰ τὴν τῶν νόμων ἀκολουθίαν.
thought_title: Refusing to leave true worship for impiety
orientation: Rusticus the prefect questions Justin about going up to heaven and then orders all the prisoners together to offer sacrifice to the gods.
pass_a_gloss: The prefect says to Justin. Listen, you who are called learned and who think you know true teachings. If after being scourged you are beheaded, are you persuaded that you are about to go up into heaven. Justin said. I hope to have its dwellings, if I endure these things. For I know that to all who have lived in this way there remains the gift from God until the fulfillment of the whole world. Rusticus the prefect said. Do you then suppose that you will go up into the heavens, about to receive some rewards. Justin said. I do not suppose, but I know and have been fully assured. Rusticus the prefect said. For the rest let us come to the matter lying before us and pressing. Having come together therefore with one mind offer sacrifice to the gods. Justin said. No one thinking rightly falls away from true worship into impiety. Rusticus the prefect said. If you do not obey, you will be punished mercilessly. Justin said. What we have as prayer is to be punished for the sake of our Lord Jesus Christ and to be saved, because this will become for us salvation and boldness before the more fearful and worldwide judgment seat of our master and savior. And in the same way also the remaining martyrs said. Do what you wish. For we are Christians and to idols we do not offer sacrifice. Rusticus the prefect pronounced saying. Those who were not willing to offer sacrifice to the gods and to yield to the order of the emperor, after being scourged let them be led away, paying the penalty of beheading according to the sequence of the laws.

pass_b_english: The prefect said to Justin, “Listen, you who are called learned and claim to know the true teachings. If you are scourged and then beheaded, are you convinced that you will go up to heaven?” Justin said, “I hope to have a home there if I endure these things. For I know that the gift from God remains for all who have lived in this way until the fulfillment of the whole world.”

Rusticus the prefect said, “So you suppose that you will go up to the heavens and receive some rewards in return?” Justin said, “I do not suppose it. I know it and am fully assured of it.” Rusticus the prefect said, “Now let us turn to the pressing matter before us. Join together with one mind and offer sacrifice to the gods.” Justin said, “No one of sound mind moves from true worship into impiety.” Rusticus the prefect said, “If you do not obey, you will be punished without mercy.” Justin said, “Our prayer is to be punished for the sake of our Lord Jesus Christ and so be saved, because this will become for us salvation and boldness before the judge at the most fearful and universal judgment seat of our Master and Savior.” The other witnesses said likewise, “Do what you please. For we are Christians, and to idols we do not offer sacrifice.”

Rusticus the prefect passed sentence, saying, “Those who have refused to offer sacrifice to the gods and to yield to the emperor’s order are to be scourged and led away to pay the capital penalty by beheading, as the laws direct.”
